assessments.reasoning: The named category section admits a property declaration and excludes added instance storage and synthesized accessors in that setting. The class extension section states that an extension compiled with the original class permits properties and instance variables.

challenge.method: Compare the exact named category and class extension passages with the explicit source-availability condition and the separate method collision warning.
challenge.results: A regular category can declare a property against an existing class, and its declaration alone adds no instance storage. The documented extension case relies on the original class source. A method collision has a separate undefined choice and supplies no additional storage rule.

limitations: The extension premise requires access to and compilation with the original class. External storage, framework-only extension, and method precedence have separate scopes.
